source.from: R1.templateFromLayers of the processed item's layers and skin shadow

trim.rule: K.seamBands: the strip between the cut edge and the seam line the cut item draws parallel to it (D-352)
trim.why: the neckline is a separate binding with a drawn stitch line; the armholes have only a faint line about 5 px in (a band there is not visible at app size and risks a ragged edge) and the hem is a turned hem in the same fabric, so they keep the body fabric
trim.revisionWhy: D-354: the seam as one smooth curve over all the region's columns, and the band's soft edge

print.boxFrom: the box on C, unchanged (its safe-area clearance on this cut is measured)

shadow.split: arms where C's arm alpha >= 128, body elsewhere on C's body (D-242)

hemJunction.drawn: after the shoes, before the bottom (the hip seam's place)

oneTimeWork: the contract itself: source item, no seams (sleeveless), the warp and print box copied from the tee

D-343: tracing which of C's base pixels the outfit check finds open beside the tank (a 1-2 px outline sliver along the side, invisible on the background, and a notch at each hem corner where the bottom's side starts) and four variants on four bottoms (sweater hip seam, none, inked side strip, shifted side) before the hem junction

the hem junction's two numbers: the outline band (3 px; 2 px leaves the right side unjoined) and the rows below C's shorts top (80, the hip seam's); C's base top below the hem joins it (else 1-4 px enclosed holes between the junction and the bottom)

the junction's alpha: opaque in the first 24 rows below each hem corner (the long trousers leave their fill transparent inside their contour at the left hip, rows 784-806, so C's soft alpha showed a 1 px light seam), C's own soft alpha below (all-opaque drew a hard stepped edge outside the trousers at the right hip, rows 800-836)
D-345: the fade (10 rows), tried on four outfits at 1:1, x2 and app size before the family check
D-352: the trim regions (panel, edge, x range, search depth) read once from the cut item at x4; the seam itself is found by the rule
D-354: no new hand-entered data; the edge rules are shared (trim.revision 2, edges.rim)
